dimensions.assessment: Directly affects the entire active-duty, reserve, civilian, and retired workforce of the Coast Guard, academy cadets, commercial shipping and merchant mariners, vessel owners and operators, and communities surrounding Coast Guard installations.
dimensions.evidence: amends-- (1) in subsection (a) by striking 44,500 for each of fiscal years 2022 and 2023 and inserting 50,000 for each of fiscal years 2025 and 2026, 55,000 for fiscal year 2027, and 60,000 for each of fiscal years 2028 and 2029

dimensions.assessment: Imposes major organizational restructuring, changes military personnel end strengths and benefits, modifies legal and administrative processes for handling misconduct and criminal offenses, and significantly adjusts training and credentialing requirements.
dimensions.evidence: There is a Secretary of the Coast Guard, appointed from civilian life by the President, by and with the advice and consent of the Senate.

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes billions of dollars in appropriations for Coast Guard operations, acquisition, construction, and retired pay for fiscal years 2025 through 2029.
dimensions.evidence: (i) $11,287,500,000 for fiscal year 2025; (ii) $11,851,875,000 for fiscal year 2026; (iii) $13,500,000,000 for fiscal year 2027; (iv) $14,500,000,000 for fiscal year 2028; and (v) $15,500,000,000 for fiscal year 2029.

dimensions.assessment: Amends multiple titles of the United States Code (including Title 14, Title 46, and Title 31), establishes new federal agency positions, advisory committees, pilot programs, and detailed statutory requirements for agency operations and oversight.
dimensions.evidence: To authorize appropriations for the Coast Guard, to establish the Secretary of the Coast Guard, and for other purposes.

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent statutory changes to the organization and authorities of the Coast Guard alongside multi-year funding authorizations and pilot programs extending through fiscal year 2029 and beyond.
dimensions.evidence: ending on December 31, 2065, not more than 50 percent of the unlicensed seamen on a vessel described in paragraph (1) may be aliens referred to in subparagraph (B) or (C)

card.summary: S. 1071, titled the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 and designated as Public Law No. 119-60, establishes the policies, authorizations, and funding levels for U.S. national defense programs, military construction, Department of Energy national security programs, intelligence activities, and maritime and Coast Guard operations. The legislation spans eight divisions covering defense acquisitions, authorizations for foreign affairs and intelligence, Coast Guard management and maritime safety reforms, security policies regarding foreign nations and illicit trafficking, and various other administrative matters.

card.label: S. 524
card.summary: The Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025 authorizes appropriations for the U.S. Coast Guard for fiscal years 2025 and 2026, sets authorized levels of military strength and training, modifies acquisition and procurement rules, and establishes numerous policies and programs relating to Coast Guard personnel, the Coast Guard Academy, vessel safety, oil pollution response, and sexual assault and harassment prevention. Additionally, the legislation amends laws concerning merchant mariner credentials, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, and the South Pacific Tuna Treaty.
card.title: Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025 sets funding levels for the U.S. Coast Guard from fiscal year 2025 through 2029, authorizes military end-strength levels and training, creates a new civilian-led Office of the Secretary of the Coast Guard, and updates organizational authorities, acquisitions, personnel policies, vessel safety rules, and oil pollution response protocols.

affected_groups.effect: Impacts pay, family leave policies, behavioral health resources, training requirements, career flexibility programs, and policies concerning sexual assault and misconduct responses.
affected_groups.group: Coast Guard personnel and military members

affected_groups.effect: Changes credentialing requirements, examination procedures, sea service substitution rules, vessel safety regulations, and reporting obligations.
Alters administrative oversight, room security mechanisms, transfer policies for victims of sexual assault, and mandatory training and reporting standards.

key_provisions: Authorizes appropriations for the Coast Guard for fiscal years 2025 through 2029, including funds for operations, construction, and retired pay.
Establishes a Presidentially appointed, Senate-confirmed civilian 'Secretary of the Coast Guard' to head the service under the Secretary of the department in which it operates.
Increases authorized levels of active-duty military strength for the Coast Guard up to 60,000 by fiscal year 2029.
Revises merchant mariner credentialing requirements, training substitutions, and updates the examination review process.
Enhances policies, reporting requirements, and prevention programs regarding sexual assault, sexual harassment, and other misconduct across the Coast Guard and the Coast Guard Academy.
Establishes new safety and security regulations, reporting mandates, and pilot programs relating to uncrewed maritime systems, icebreaking, and environmental protection.
missing_information: Specific details on the exact organizational placement and operational transition timelines of the newly created Secretary of the Coast Guard position prior to further study and reporting.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Coast Guard Authorization Act of 2025 sets funding levels for the U.S. Coast Guard from fiscal year 2025 through 2029, authorizes military end-strength levels and training, creates a new civilian-led Office of the Secretary of the Coast Guard, and updates organizational authorities, acquisitions, personnel policies, vessel safety rules, and oil pollution response protocols.
summary_detail.significance: The bill represents a sweeping reauthorization and organizational restructuring of the U.S. Coast Guard, impacting its multi-billion-dollar budget, personnel levels, operational authorities, and internal accountability measures over a five-year period.
